'''Idoma''' (Ìdɔ́mà) is the second official language spoken in [[Benue State]] in southeast-central [[Nigeria]], by approximately one million people (2020 estimate).<ref name=e25/> The Idoma language is made up of the dialects of [[Agatu language|Agatu]], Edumoga, Otukpo, Otukpa, Orokam, Akpa Agila, Utonkon, [[Igede language|Igede]], Etilo, [[Yala language|Iyala]]. The Idoma people are predominantly hunters, farmers and fishermen. They are bordered to the north by [[Nasarawa State|Nasarawa]], south by [[Cross River State|Cross River]], east by [[Taraba state|Taraba]] and west by [[Enugu State|Enugu]] and [[Kogi State|Kogi]] States.<ref name=e25/>
